previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis and sphincter of Oddi dysfunction was admitted for recurrent epigastric abdominal pain and nausea. She presented with poor oral intake and was initially managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV pain and nausea medications. Her lipase levels trended downward, indicating improvement in pancreatic inflammation. She was transitioned to oral pain control, advanced to a full diet, and remained stable without further nausea or pain. A brief episode of hypotension resolved with fluid bolus and pain control. Constipation was managed with scheduled stool softeners and laxatives. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with her GI specialist and primary care provider, continue her home medications, and monitor for recurrence of symptoms.
problems: Other specified disorders of biliary tract

Brief Hospital Course:
Assessment and plan:
# Acute on chronic pancreatitis, likely ___ Sphincter of Oddi 
dysfunction: This is very typical of her prior bouts of 
abdominal pain. She turned around very quickly this admission. 
ERCP was consulted and felt there was no need for additional 
diagnostics given her normal LFTs on presentation. She was given 
some IVF, slight bowel rest, and her home medication regimen, 
and improved. She tolerated a regular diet for lunch prior to 
discharge.

# Hypotension: Has had intermittent bouts of hypotension in past 
in setting of nausea and medication use, typically responsive to 
fluids. This did not occur this admission, with SBPs stable in 
her normal range of ___. She was placed on maintenance 
fluids while resting her bowels the day and night of admission.

# Constipation: Has been an issue during prior hospitalizations. 
She was nondistended but I did get a sense of some fecal loading 
on exam. She was discharged on her home bowel regimen.

# Anxiety, depression, PTSD: She feels safe here. Continued home
